title: FiniteSumSmoothNonconvex.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization permits nonconvex components and objectives. F has a global lower bound lower with F(x0)−lower≤Δ; no minimizer or convexity is required.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Every reply is an exact component gradient, for every call index and oracle seed. There is no oracle error or stochastic noise assumption; algorithmic randomization is allowed.

oracle.label: component_gradient
oracle.details: A query chooses any component i and point x and receives ∇f_i(x). Each individual evaluation counts as one oracle call.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/FiniteSumSmoothNonconvex.lean: spec.Query, spec.Reply, spec.admissible; LongTails/Template.lean: execute and Convergence

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Average squared smoothness: (1/n)Σ_i‖∇f_i(x)−∇f_i(y)‖²≤L²‖x−y‖². A common componentwise L-Lipschitz bound is not required. The ambient space is an arbitrary complete real inner-product space. All parameters E,n,L,Δ,ε,x0 are public, with L>0, Δ≥0, ε>0.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm_squared
accuracy.details: Output X∈E must be measurable, its squared objective-gradient norm integrable, and E‖∇F(X)‖²≤ε². No last-iterate requirement is imposed.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: Accuracy is in expectation under the joint algorithm and oracle seed law. Oracle cost is bounded for every seed by the prescribed fixed budget.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: This is the established smooth nonconvex finite-sum stationarity benchmark with exact component gradients and average squared smoothness, formulated in a general Hilbert space.

descriptionHtml:
Finite-Sum Nonconvex Optimization

We consider minimizing F(x)=n−1∑i=1nfi(x) on a real Hilbert space E, where n≥1 and the differentiable components fi:E→R may be nonconvex. Their gradients satisfy a mean-square Lipschitz bound with constant L>0. At a given starting point x0∈E, the objective lies within Δ≥0 of a global lower bound. The oracle returns ∇fi(x) at a queried index i and point x. For ε>0, the goal is a measurable output x¯∈E with EP[∥∇F(x¯)∥2]≤ε2, where P is the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

The optimization problem is infx∈EF(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E, which is equipped with a measurable structure. The algorithm receives E, n, L, Δ, ε, and x0.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Mean-square smoothness). Each component fi is Fréchet differentiable everywhere on E, and 1n∑i=1n∥∇fi(x)−∇fi(y)∥2≤L2∥x−y∥2,x,y∈E. Consequently, the objective gradient is ∇F(x)=1n∑i=1n∇fi(x).

Assumption 2 (Lower bound and initial gap). There exists ℓ∈R such that F(x)≥ℓfor every x∈E,F(x0)−ℓ≤Δ.

Queries may use any index i∈{1,…,n} and any point x∈E; each query returns one exact component gradient. After the allotted oracle calls, the output x¯ must be measurable, its squared gradient norm must be integrable under P, and it must satisfy EP[∥∇F(x¯)∥2]≤ε2.

theorems.referencesHtml:
• Cong Fang, Chris Junchi Li, Zhouchen Lin, Tong Zhang. SPIDER: Near-Optimal Non-Convex Optimization via Stochastic Path-Integrated Differential Estimator. 2018. Complexity: O(n+nLΔ/ε2) exact component-gradient calls, including initialization and batches, with fixed cost; SPIDER-SFO obtains E∥∇F(X)∥≤ε.
  • Lam M. Nguyen, Marten van Dijk, Dzung T. Phan, Phuong Ha Nguyen, Tsui-Wei Weng, Jayant R. Kalagnanam. Finite-Sum Smooth Optimization with SARAH. 2019 preprint, version 2. Complexity: O(n+nLΔ/ε2) exact component-gradient calls, including full-gradient initialization, refreshes, and paired evaluations, with fixed cost; modified SARAH obtains E∥∇F(X)∥2≤ε2.
  • Zhize Li, Hongyan Bao, Xiangliang Zhang, Peter Richtárik. PAGE: A Simple and Optimal Probabilistic Gradient Estimator for Nonconvex Optimization. 2021. Complexity: O(n+nLΔ/ε2) expected exact component-gradient calls, including initialization, refresh batches, and paired evaluations; PAGE obtains E∥∇F(X)∥2≤ε2.
theorems.formulaHtml: 5⋅n+⌈20⋅n⋅L⋅Δε2⌉+

comparisonHtml:
On a real Hilbert space E equipped with a measurable structure, let F=n−1∑i=1nfi, with differentiable fi and n≥1. Assume n−1∑i∥∇fi(x)−∇fi(y)∥2≤L2∥x−y∥2 for all x,y, and F≥ℓ with F(x0)−ℓ≤Δ, where L>0, Δ≥0. The oracle returns exact component gradients. For ε>0, the target is a measurable output X with integrable squared gradient and ∫∥∇F(X(ω))∥2dP(ω)≤ε2, where P is the algorithm’s randomization law. Convexity and attainment of the infimum are not assumed.

Finite-sum nonconvex optimization under mean-squared smoothness (FiniteSumSmoothNonconvex).
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) RecursiveGradientNonconvex (Ours) (review) O(n+nLΔε2) deterministic calls.
(2) Minibatch SARAH (Nguyen et al. 2019, Thm. 2, Cor. 3). E=Rd. O(n+nLΔε2) deterministic calls; batch and epoch lengths ≍n. (1): Matches known rate, formalized in Lean. Scope: Hilbert spaces. With-replacement instead of without-replacement batches; no rate or tuning-knowledge improvement.
(3) SpiderBoost (Wang et al. 2020, Thm. 1; App. G, Thm. 9). E=Rd; each ∇fi is L-Lipschitz. O(n+nLΔε2) deterministic calls; squared-gradient guarantee from App. G. (1): Scope: mean-squared smoothness instead of componentwise smoothness; Hilbert spaces. Matches rate on the common setup. The smoothness relaxation is already covered by (2).
(4) PAGE (Li et al. 2021, Thm. 1, Cor. 2; App. A.1, Eq. (23)). E=Rd; F∗=minF in the stated gap. O(n+nLΔε2) expected calls; squared-gradient guarantee from App. A.1. (1): Deterministic rather than expected call budget, at matched order on the common setup; this budget guarantee already holds for (2).

Abbr: n: number of components; L: mean-squared smoothness bound; ℓ: objective lower bound; Δ: initial gap bound; ε: root-mean-square gradient tolerance. Calls count individual component-gradient evaluations, including full refreshes and two evaluations per sampled difference. Prior-work gaps are bounded by Δ on the common setup; ≍ denotes equality up to universal factors.

import LongTails.Setups.FiniteSumSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.BigOperators.Expect

open MeasureTheory
open scoped BigOperators

namespace LongTails.Setups.FiniteSumSmoothNonconvex

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  E : Type u
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  n : ℕ
  [nonzero : NeZero n]
  L : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.linearE Params.completeE Params.measurableE
  Params.nonzero

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := Fin p.n → p.E → ℝ
  Query p := Fin p.n × p.E
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput p := p
  valid p := 0 < p.L ∧ 0 ≤ p.Δ ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p f oracle :=
    (∀ i x, HasGradientAt (f i) (gradient (f i) x) x) ∧
    (∀ k seed i x, HasGradientAt (f i) (oracle.answer k (0, (i, x)) seed) x) ∧
    (∀ x y, (𝔼 i, ‖gradient (f i) x - gradient (f i) y‖ ^ 2) ≤
      p.L ^ 2 * ‖x - y‖ ^ 2) ∧
    (∃ lower : ℝ, (∀ x, lower ≤ LongTails.Setups.FiniteSumSmoothAndConvex.objective f x) ∧
      LongTails.Setups.FiniteSumSmoothAndConvex.objective f p.x0 - lower ≤ p.Δ)
  successful p f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
    Integrable (fun ω => ‖gradient (LongTails.Setups.FiniteSumSmoothAndConvex.objective f) (output ω)‖ ^ 2)
      (P : Measure _) ∧
    (∫ ω, ‖gradient (LongTails.Setups.FiniteSumSmoothAndConvex.objective f) (output ω)‖ ^ 2 ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ p.ε ^ 2

end LongTails.Setups.FiniteSumSmoothNonconvex
